Posts on a member's profile and on the company pages they admin.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own LinkedIn account once, in the Gateway, and every app that asks for it uses that connection. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

- **Make the OAuth app here:** [linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps)
- **Settings:** `LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID`, `LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET`
- **Added with:** `pnpm everyapp provider add --oauth linkedin`

### Redirect URI

Register this at the provider:

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/linkedin/callback
```

`<your gateway>` is your Gateway's address, like `apps.example.com`.

An app that runs the sign-in itself lists its own callbacks under `redirectPaths` in its manifest entry; register those too, as `https://<app>.<your gateway><path>`. `pnpm everyapp provider show linkedin` prints every one.

### Make the OAuth app

Add the Sign In with LinkedIn and Share on LinkedIn products to the app; company pages need the Community Management API. Refresh tokens come to approved partners only. Not yet tried against a live connect.

1. Open [linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps) and create an OAuth app (sometimes called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Allow the scopes behind the sets your apps use (the table below), and no others.
4. Copy the client ID and the client secret. The secret is often shown once.

Steps for this provider are brief. [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20LinkedIn) to request a full guide.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp provider add --oauth linkedin
pnpm everyapp secret set LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID LINKEDIN_CLIENT_SECRET
```

Each value goes in at a hidden prompt. Or, as an owner or admin, paste the client in **Manage workspace → Providers → Add OAuth provider**.

### Scope sets

Apps ask for named sets, never raw scopes, and the Gateway holds each app to the sets it declared.

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | LinkedIn account (who you are) | `openid`, `profile` |
| `posts.write` | Posts on your profile | `openid`, `profile`, `w_member_social` |
| `pages.write` | Company pages you admin (read and post) | `rw_organization_admin`, `w_organization_social`, `r_organization_social` |

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  linkedin: { access: "write", scopes: ["posts.write"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp provider show linkedin` shows the client as set, and the redirect URI.
- Open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect LinkedIn**. You land back in the Gateway, connected.
- `pnpm everyapp provider connections` lists who has connected.
